title: High Court halts public university admission tests until 31 December
excerpt: The order follows a petition for students who failed two HSC subjects. The government plans retests for them within a month.
content:
The High Court on Wednesday (18 November) stopped all public university admission tests until 31 December, bdnews24.com reported. A bench of Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice SM Iftekhar Uddin Mahmud gave the order after a preliminary hearing on a writ petition filed by lawyer Kamrun Nahar Mahmud.

The petition says students who failed two subjects in this year's HSC exams are being shut out of admission tests. It also challenges universities for ignoring a University Grants Commission directive to start tests on 1 January. About 450,000 students failed two subjects, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported.

Deputy Attorney General Mohammad Mohsin Kabir confirmed the order and said the government would hold retests within a month for students who failed.

Why it matters

The ruling affects the timing of university entry for hundreds of thousands of young people, and a fairer chance for those who failed two subjects. Education and youth NGOs that support first-generation and low-income students may need to adjust coaching, scholarship and counselling plans.

What to watch

The date of the HSC retests, a full hearing on the petition, and new admission schedules from the universities.
